title: Semantic shingle prober and graceful rollback orchestrator
author: Lena Patel
release_notes: Add a semantic shingle prober (targeted mini-evals based on embedding shingles) and a rollback orchestrator that applies backpressure to CI replay to reduce noisy rollbacks. Improves prompt-set regression precision and reduces false-positive gating.
description:
Motivation: CI early-warning gates were generating a high volume of noisy failures for long prompt-sets where failures clustered around overlapping semantic fragments. This PR introduces a 'semantic shingle' prober that extracts embedding-based shingles (semantic n-grams) from prompt sets, runs focused mini-evals across those shingles, and computes a precision-weighted failure score. The goal is twofold: 1) increase the signal-to-noise of regression detections by isolating semantic hotspots, and 2) provide a graduated rollback orchestration that applies replay backpressure instead of immediate full-suite rollbacks to avoid thrashing on intermittent instability.

What this changes (high level): Add a new prober module that performs shingle extraction using existing embeddings, an orchestration hook that schedules targeted mini-evals and aggregates a precision-weighted signal, and a CI-side rollback orchestrator that can: delay full replays, queue progressive mini-eval replays, and escalate to a full rollback only when aggregated severity passes configured thresholds.

Checklist: [x] implement semantic shingle extractor and sampler [x] implement targeted mini-eval runner with deterministic seeds [x] add orchestration hook and state tracking [x] unit + integration tests for edge cases (short prompts, high duplication) [x] add runbook notes to docs/ci/runbooks.md [x] benchmark against existing random-probe baseline (results below)

Benchmarks: On a 1.2k-prompt internal SLO set, precision of flagged regressions improved from 0.62 -> 0.81 (fewer false positives), and the number of full-suite replays triggered by the CI gate dropped by ~47% in our simulated backlog run. Median additional CI latency introduced by the orchestrator was +3s (the orchestrator runs async and applies backpressure before expensive replays).

Commits summary: 1) Initialize semantic shingle prober and sampling api (semantics: cosine similarity cutoff, shingle size heuristics). 2) Add targeted mini-eval runner and deterministic replay wrapper. 3) Implement rollback_orchestrator with backpressure queue and escalation policy. 4) Integrate with ci/hooks and add config knobs (shingle_size, similarity_threshold, escalation_window). 5) Tests + docs + small refactors based on review feedback.

Changed areas / files (high-level): eval_harness/probers/semantic_shingle.py -- new core prober that produces shingle cohorts; eval_harness/runner/mini_eval_runner.py -- targeted runner used by the prober; ci/hooks/rollback_orchestrator.py -- new orchestrator that listens to gated failures and implements backpressure; ci/config/shingle_policy.yaml.example -- new config knobs for ops; tests/test_semantic_shingle.py, tests/test_orchestrator.py -- unit + integration tests; docs/ci/runbooks.md -- added operator guidance and escalation matrix. Small refactors: moved embedding cache helper into eval_harness/utils/embedding_cache.py to avoid duplication.

Small illustrative snippet (semantic shingle heuristic): """# pseudocode
for prompt in prompt_set:
  tokens = tokenize(prompt)
  for window in sliding_windows(tokens, size=shingle_size):
    emb = embed(window)
    assign_to_cluster(closest_centroid, threshold=similarity_threshold)
"""
